posts.author: yonderdavid.bsky.social
posts.text: So there was a simple pipeline repetition version, but I could hardly inflict it on you or the innocent bystanders who might happen upon it. …
posts.note: Read aloud by Sibyl (line reply-1), cut after its first sentence; the card shows only what is read, with the ellipsis. The second sentence is what the wordless stretch draws.

posts.author: yonderdavid.bsky.social
posts.text: By such applications of beeswax and string I obtained this version, which one might call distinguishable from a polished one. But the bowing is improved.
posts.alt: Two chimera-vocal-synth heads sing, with voices otherwise synthesized, the folk song "Factory Girl." They are accompanied by two fiddles and a cello, whose sound derives from physical simulation of those instruments.
posts.note: Read aloud whole by Sibyl across two consecutive beats (reply-2a, reply-2b), split at its own sentence break; the card shows the post whole. Its video is known only by its alt text, which the studio sketch is drawn from.

posts.author: yonderdavid.bsky.social
posts.text: I probably should have asked if you meant the feminine-voiced version of it, but at any rate that's what I attempted and ran into frustrations with the synth. It tends to make feminine voices sound like a masculine voice in falsetto, with either a reedy or a honky quality.
posts.note: Not shown or read. The first post of the three-post reply; the digest parent of the post read at reply-1.

posts.author: yonderdavid.bsky.social
posts.text: Very well, it's arguably still chimera-vocal-synth week, so I can fix that. The cat voice sim joins a quartet and instruments that get their sound from physical models.
posts.alt: A quartet of chimera-vocal-synth voices, plus a physically simulated feline voice, sing "Poor Wayfaring Stranger," accompanied by physically simulated guitar and fiddle.
posts.note: Not shown or read. The first folk-song video, the basis of the opening line.
